questions.q: In the Procure-to-Pay process, what comes immediately after the Purchase Order?
questions.explain: The order is Requisition, Purchase Order, Receipt, Invoice, Payment — the Receipt confirms the goods physically arrived.

options: Matching three different suppliers' prices before choosing one
Comparing the Purchase Order, the Receipt, and the supplier Invoice before approving payment
Matching three customer orders into one shipment
questions.explain: The three-way match compares the PO, the receipt, and the invoice so a company doesn't pay for goods it never ordered or never received.

questions.q: In Order-to-Cash, what triggers the Accounts Receivable invoice?
options: The customer calling to ask for one
What was actually shipped to the customer
The end of the fiscal year
questions.explain: The invoice is generated based on what was actually shipped/fulfilled, not simply on the original order.

questions.q: Which business process would a software company's fictional example scenario of 'a customer orders finished goods, and the warehouse ships them' belong to?
questions.explain: That scenario — sales order through fulfillment, invoice, and cash receipt — is Order-to-Cash.

questions.q: Where do both Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash ultimately post their accounting impact?
options: A spreadsheet maintained by the Controller
questions.explain: Whatever module a process starts in, it eventually produces an accounting entry that lands in the General Ledger.
